title: Influence of the Néel vector on the bulk electronic structure of MnTe measured from the $(1 \bar1 00)$ surface
authors: D. A. Usanov, A. B. Hellenes, S. Hahn, M. Leandersson, J. Osiecki, K. Uhlířová, D. Evtushinsky, L. Šmejkal, T. Jungwirth, J. H. Dil
abstract: Altermagnetism gives rise to momentum-dependent spin splitting without net magnetization. Here, we use angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) to investigate bulk $α$-MnTe single crystals cleaved along the $(1\bar{1}00)$ plane - an orientation that preserves the compensated magnetic symmetry at the surface and substantially reduces surface effects and $k_z$ broadening. We resolve the three-dimensional bulk band structure with markedly enhanced spectral clarity. The $d$-wave band splitting, driven by the altermagnetic order and spin-orbit coupling in the $\mathbfΓ-\mathbf{K}-\mathbf{M}$ nodal plane, shows a perfect match to theoretical predictions. We further establish that the valence-band maximum occurs near the $\mathbf{A}$ point, identifying the corresponding hole pockets as the states governing the transport properties. Spatially resolved measurements reveal systematic variations of the band dispersion along $\mathbfΓ-\mathbf{K}$ and $\mathbf{A}-\mathbf{L}$, associated with different pinning of the Néel vector at the surface. Our results establish a surface-sensitive route to resolving the bulk altermagnetic electronic structure of MnTe and provide direct spectroscopic evidence for Néel-vector-dependent band splitting.
summary: This paper uses ARPES on cleaved (1$ ar{1}$00) MnTe surfaces to study how the Néel vector dictates the bulk electronic structure. The researchers observed a characteristic spin splitting in the electronic bands, confirming altermagnetism. This work establishes a powerful surface-sensitive technique to map out the magnetic influence on electronic properties in correlated materials.
main_problem: The study investigates how the Néel vector influences the bulk electronic structure of MnTe, focusing on the phenomenon of altermagnetism.
main_result: The ARPES measurements confirm the altermagnetic nature of MnTe, showing a characteristic band splitting whose magnitude varies systematically depending on the orientation of the Néel vector at the surface.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) was used on cleaved (1$ ar{1}$00) surfaces, complemented by Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations.
model_or_system: The physical system is $\alpha$-MnTe single crystals. The measurements probe the electronic band structure, specifically looking for momentum-dependent spin splitting driven by altermagnetic order and spin-orbit coupling.
key_observables: Momentum-dependent spin splitting (d-wave splitting), band dispersion along $\Gamma-\text{K}$ and $\text{A}-	ext{L}$, and the variation of this splitting with the magnetic domain orientation.
important_parameters: Temperature (18 K), crystal surface orientation ($(1\bar{1}00)$), and the direction of the Néel vector ($\vec{N}$).
main_assumptions: The $(1\bar{1}00)$ surface is assumed to minimize surface effects and $k_z$ broadening, allowing for a surface-sensitive view of the bulk altermagnetic structure.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the crystal structure and Brillouin zones, showing ARPES data along $\Gamma-\text{K}$ and $\Gamma-\text{A}$ directions, comparing measured band maps to DFT predictions and highlighting domain-dependent splitting.
paper_structure: The paper details the experimental setup using ARPES on the specific crystal surface, presents the spectroscopic evidence for altermagnetic splitting, correlates the observed splitting magnitude with different magnetic domain orientations (Néel vector pinning), and concludes by establishing a surface-sensitive route to map the bulk electronic structure.
why_interesting: The work provides direct spectroscopic evidence of magnetic ordering effects (altermagnetism) on electronic bands, which is highly relevant to understanding correlated materials where magnetic structure dictates electronic properties.
